Hey Everyone 👋 I live in the terminal. I write code in Neovim and use lazygit, lazydocker and other TUIs every day. But each time I had to work with AWS, I had to leave the terminal for the console or type long CLI commands just to answer simple questions. Which instances are running? What is in this bucket? Did that Lambda deploy? I wanted the lazygit feel for AWS too, so I built my own: Lazy AWS. What it does: - Browse EC2, ECS, ECR, S3 and Lambda in one terminal UI - Filter lists, see related resources and read the full JSON details - Run actions such as stopping an instance or uploading a file, always with a confirmation step Try it in 10 seconds: $ brew install capybara-brain346/tap/lazyaws $ lazyaws

results.title: Who audits the bots?
results.content:
Appwrite Sites is the platform’s new hosting arm. Point it at a static or server-rendered repo, click deploy, hook up your domain, and you’re live, with SSL, previews, and templates included. Think Vercel vibes, minus the closed source.
 Gadget is a browser IDE that shows up with the boring bits already handled: database, auth, testing, hosting, and an assistant that can scaffold routes or tables when you get lazy. Start a project, write code, hit deploy, and the app goes live on Gadget’s cloud—no AWS spelunking required.
